questions.q: A 20 ton truck is travelling along a curved path of radius 240 m . If the center of gravity of the truck above the ground is 2 m and the distance between its wheels is 1.5 m , the maximum speed of the truck with which it can travel without toppling over is (Acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution:
Let the maximum speed of the truck with which it can travel without toppling $=V_{\max }=$ ?
Here $\frac{m V_{\max }^2 \mathrm{~h}}{\mathrm{R}}=\mathrm{mg} \frac{\mathrm{d}}{2}$ where $\mathrm{h}=$ height of centre of gravity of truck above the ground, $R=$ radius of curved path, $d=$ distance between the wheels of truck
$\therefore \mathrm{V}_{\max }^2=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{Rgd}}{2 \mathrm{~h}}}=\sqrt{\frac{240 \times 10 \times 1.5}{2 \times 2}}=\sqrt{60 \times 15}=30 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$

If the maximum permissible speed of the car to avoid slipping is twice the optimum speed of the car to avoid the wear and tear of the tyres, then the coefficient of static friction between the wheels of the car and the road is
questions.solution:
Maximum speed $V_{\max }=\sqrt{\frac{r g(\mu+\tan \theta)}{1-\mu \tan \theta}}$
and optimum speed $V_{\mathrm{o}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{rg} \tan \theta}$
Given $\theta=45^{\circ}$ and $V_{\max }=2 V_0\sqrt{\frac{\operatorname{rg}(\mu+\tan \theta)}{1-\mu \tan \theta}}=2 \sqrt{\operatorname{rg} \tan \theta}$
Squaring both sides $\frac{(\mu+\tan \theta)}{(1-\mu \tan \theta)}=4 \tan \theta\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{\mu+\tan 45^{\circ}}{1-\mu \tan 45^{\circ}}=4 \tan 45^{\circ} \Rightarrow \frac{\mu+1}{1-\mu}=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \mu+1=4-4 \mu \Rightarrow 5 \mu=3 \therefore \mu=\frac{3}{5}=0.6
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: For mass $\mathrm{W}_1$ \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{a}-\mathrm{W}_1 a_0=\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \\ & \mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{a}-\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~g}=\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \\ & \mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{a}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \end{aligned} For mass $\mathrm{W}_2$ \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{o}}=\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{~g} \\ & \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{~g}=\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{~g} \\ & \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{T}-2 \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{~g} \end{aligned} Adding equation (i) and (ii), We have \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{W}_2 \mathrm{a}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-2 \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{~g} \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~g}\left(\mathrm{~W}_1-\mathrm{W}_2\right)}{\mathrm{W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2} \end{aligned} Put this value in equation (i) \begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_1 \times \frac{2 \mathrm{~g}\left(\mathrm{~W}_1-\mathrm{W}_2\right)}{\mathrm{W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \\ & \frac{2 \mathrm{gW}_1^2}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2}-\frac{2 \mathrm{gW}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\mathrm{T} \\ & \mathrm{T}=2 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~g}-\frac{2 \mathrm{gW}_1^2}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2}+\frac{2 \mathrm{gW}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2} \\ & =\frac{2 \mathrm{~g}\left[\mathrm{~W}_1^2+\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2-\mathrm{W}_1^2+\mathrm{W}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2\right]}{\mathrm{W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2} \\ & =\frac{4 \mathrm{~W}_1 \mathrm{~W}_2 \mathrm{~g}}{\mathrm{~W}_1+\mathrm{W}_2} \end{aligned}

When the lift accelerates with acceleration $a$, then the normal reaction force $N$ by the elevator on the person is given as
$\therefore N-m g=m a$ (where, $m$ is the actual mass of that person)
When the lift deaccelerates with acceleration $a$ then, $m g-N=m a$

(i), we get, $80 g=m(g+a)=m\left(g+\frac{g}{9}\right)$ \begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow & 80 g=\frac{10 g}{9} m \\ \Rightarrow & m=\frac{80 \times 9}{10}=72 \mathrm{~kg} \end{array} So, the true weight of that person is $72 \mathrm{~kg}$.

questions.solution:
The four fundamental forces of nature are as follows,

(ii) Weak nuclear force which is also between nuclear particles, however its strength is low and of the order of $10^{-13}$. This force is usually found in radioactive nuclei. It is also a short range force.
(iii) Electromagnetic force which is the force between the electrically charged particles. Its strength is of the order of $10^{-2}$. But its range is very high, upto infinity.

questions.solution:
Minimum force required to move a body up a rough inclined plane
$F_1=m g(\sin \theta+\mu \cos \theta)$
Minimum force required to prevent the body from sliding down the rough inclined plane
$F_2=\mu m g \cos \theta$
According to question,
$F_1=3 F_2\begin{aligned} \therefore m g(\sin \theta+\mu \cos \theta) & =3(\mu m g \cos \theta) \\ \sin \theta+\mu \cos \theta & =3 \mu \cos \theta \\ \sin \theta & =2 \mu \cos \theta \\ \tan \theta & =2 \mu \\ & =2 \times \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & =\tan 30^{\circ} \\ \therefore \quad \theta & =30^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
